how_to_use: Each persona file holds a complete answer set and the expected outcome. A persona passes if the recommendation matches, the total and both category scores fall inside their ranges, the fired gates match exactly, the threshold rules match exactly, the exemptions match exactly, and the suggestion include/exclude assertions hold. Suggestion assertions are against the TRIGGERED set, not the 3-5 displayed. Separately, scripts/check-personas.mts applies one global invariant to every persona with no per-persona assertion needed: the DISPLAYED suggestion count must land between meta.selection.min_shown and max_shown (3-5) in config/suggestions/high-b-to-low-c.json. Run with: node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check-personas.mts high-b-to-low-c

field_notes.rules_expected: Threshold rules that actually applied and constrained the result. Named '<rule_id>:<question_id_or_category>' where a rule is driven by one answer or one category. Note the engine only reports a Ready-path threshold rule when the total itself reached the Ready threshold — a pilot held at Nearly ready by their total alone reports no rule. The not_yet category floors are a separate branch and ARE reported, which is why persona 08 carries one.
field_notes.exemptions_expected: Exemption ids that suppressed a rule which would otherwise have applied. Every persona here has an EMPTY exemptions list, and that is structural rather than accidental: config/scoring/high-b-to-low-c.json ships an empty thresholds.ready.unevidenced_core_checks.exemptions array on purpose, as mid-b-to-high-b.json does, and for a stronger reason — no source at this step offers a soaring-only route to decline. See the negative check about carried-over exemptions below.
field_notes.critical_check_floor_ordering: The engine breaks on the first failing question in thresholds.ready.critical_check_floor.questions, so at most one 'critical_check_floor:*' string is ever emitted and WHICH one depends on list order. The order in this step's config is deliberate (most-to-least step-specific, with reading_the_day and reserve_familiarity last because they are the softest-sourced members). Only persona 03 trips a critical_check_floor member at all — every other pilot with a failing member is gated first, and gates short-circuit.

persona_count_note: Nine files, the upper end of the 6-9 the brief asks for. This rubric needs it: it has 12 gates, 10 Ready-blockers, two questions that exist at no step below (xc_experience, effort_already_invested), one gate that exists at no step below (collapse_response_entirely_untested), and one widened gate (occasional_pilot_profile). Nothing here is a near-clone. If the count ever needs trimming, the honest candidate is 09 'notyet-experienced-but-occasional', whose mechanism is a widened version of one already proven at mid-B to high-B — though it is the only persona exercising the currency gate at all, so it is the last one worth losing.
expected_values_provenance: The score ranges in these files were computed by hand from config/scoring/high-b-to-low-c.json (skills weights total 198, psychological weights total 96, category split 0.53/0.47). The 'computed' figures below are the hand-calculated values; each persona's asserted range is roughly plus or minus four points around them to tolerate arithmetic slip. The first run of a real scorer should reproduce the 'computed' figures to within rounding; if it doesn't, check the arithmetic here before changing the engine — but if a persona's RECOMMENDATION, gates, rules or exemptions differ, the disagreement is structural and worth investigating properly. Two personas sit deliberately close to a line and should be read first if anything disagrees: persona 05 (skills a few points ABOVE the ambition gate's 55 threshold, which must keep that gate silent) and persona 07 (total a few points ABOVE the 78 Ready threshold while skills sits well BELOW the 72 floor, which is what produces the only ready_category_floor result in the set).

ready-earned-the-step.note: Raw total before clamping is 101.0; the engine clamps to 100.

note_on_distribution: The most conservative distribution of the four steps built so far (4 of 10 Ready at A to low-B, 3 of 9 at low-B to mid-B, 2 of 9 at mid-B to high-B, 2 of 9 here with one fewer Nearly ready). That is intended and it is the asymmetric-risk finding showing up in the test set rather than a drift: the sources at this boundary say plainly that getting onto a C too early costs more than staying on a B too long, and the resale asymmetry says the same thing in money. Note that four of the five Not yet personas have genuinely decent flying and score in the high fifties to low seventies — three are capped by a gate rather than by a thin score, and one (08) is capped by the psychological floor with a near-perfect skills score. That is the shape of a step where the demands are about demonstrated collapse response, currency and honest motives rather than about raw competence.

gate_coverage.thermic_hours_low_and_thin_currency: Not exercised as a FIRING gate, deliberately. Persona 03 matches its thermic band (25_50) and must NOT be gated, because he is flying weekly with 50-80 hours in the last year — that is the clause that keeps a pilot who is actively closing the gap out of the cap. The negative case is the more important one here. A synthetic unit check should confirm the gate DOES fire for the same thermic answer paired with airtime_last_12m: 10_25, or with flying_frequency: about_monthly.
gate_coverage.collapse_control_lost: Not exercised, deliberately. Persona 06 sits one band above it (froze, wing recovered itself) and is caught by the new 'collapse_response_entirely_untested' gate instead. That pair is this rubric's most important collapse distinction and the thing a reviewer should check first: freezing with no practice is capped by the NEW gate, losing control is capped by the brief's own gate, and self-practice plus freezing is only a Ready-blocker. A synthetic unit check should confirm both 'lost_control' and 'repeated_struggle' cap at Not yet on their own, whatever the practice answer.
gate_coverage.no_recent_flying: Not exercised. Persona 09 sits one band above it ('about once a month'), which is the distinction that matters at this step: no flying at all gates on its own, monthly flying needs a thin 12-month figure alongside it. Worth a synthetic unit check.
gate_coverage.unreliable_launches: Not exercised. The weakest launch answer in the set is persona 06's 'clean about half the time', which is scored rather than gated. Worth a synthetic unit check, and worth remembering the gate rests on general accident data rather than anything in this step's own file.
gate_coverage.instructor_said_wait: Not exercised. Mechanically identical to the same gate at all three steps below, where it is already proven. Worth a synthetic unit check — the message is new, so a copy review matters more than the logic.
gate_coverage.still_in_training: Not exercised. Almost certainly inert three rungs up the ladder, and flagged in config/scoring/high-b-to-low-c.json meta.owner_decisions as removable. Worth a synthetic unit check rather than a persona.

not_exercised: critical_check_floor on collapse_practice, wing_limiting_evidence, active_piloting, thermal_turn_control, response_when_rough, flying_frequency, collapse_experience, reading_the_day and reserve_familiarity. Several personas hold failing answers for these (05 fails wing_limiting_evidence at 0.1 and collapse_practice at 0.45; 06 fails active_piloting at 0.3, thermal_turn_control at 0.25, reading_the_day at 0.1, collapse_practice at 0.2, collapse_experience at 0.15 and response_when_rough at 0.2; 09 fails flying_frequency at 0.4, collapse_practice at 0.45 and wing_limiting_evidence at 0.35) but every one of them is gated first, and gates short-circuit. Each is worth a synthetic unit check: take persona 02 and change one answer at a time, which is also the cheapest way to review the nine rule_messages those cases would render. This step has more of that copy than any predecessor.

unevidenced_core_checks:thermal_turn_control. No persona answers 'I mostly soar or glide rather than thermal'. That is a deliberate gap in this set and worth closing with a synthetic check rather than a persona, because the behaviour is structurally identical to mid-b-to-high-b persona 03 (which IS a full persona there): the answer scores 0.5, passes the critical_check_floor, blocks Ready through unevidenced_core_checks, and has NO exemption. The thing to verify here is that the 'thermalling_untested' and 'local_plans_and_this_wings_purpose' suggestions both fire so the block is explained, and that the rule message's claim — that there is no reading of this step's guidance a soaring-only pilot clears — reads as plain fact rather than as a reprimand.

ready_category_floor:psychological. Not reachable from any persona here: persona 08 is the lopsided-psychological pilot and he falls through to the Not yet floor instead. A synthetic check should take persona 02 and weaken the psychological answers just enough to land between 68 and the Ready threshold.

not_yet_category_floor:skills. No persona falls below the floor of 48 except persona 06 at 32.9, who is gated first. Worth a synthetic check, and worth noting the floor rose from 45 at mid-B to high-B, so a persona sitting at 46 behaves differently here than one rung down.
conservative_backstop. No persona leaves questions blank; every persona answers all 34.
rule_coverage.owner_decision: The un-exercised threshold rules all use logic shared with the three steps below and already proven there. What is NOT covered by these personas is whether each piece of this step's rule_messages copy reads correctly in a real result — and this step has the most of that copy in the ladder (ten critical_check_floor messages, several of which name the 75-to-100-plus range and must keep presenting it as a range). Worth deciding between a few more personas and a synthetic copy-review pass.

suggestion_coverage.always_pool_sizing: config/suggestions/high-b-to-low-c.json ships FOUR 'always': true suggestions on four distinct topics (instructor, currency, transition, step_confidence), one more than min_shown. Two of them can be topic-deduped by a triggered suggestion ('stay_current_whatever_you_decide' by improve_currency or recurrency_plan, 'compensate_after_any_upgrade' by transition_plan), but dedupe replaces rather than subtracts, so the displayed count never falls. Personas 04, 08 and 09 all exercise at least one of those displacements. Every persona in this set reaches five displayed suggestions.
suggestion_coverage.thin_end_note: The thinnest trigger set here is persona 01 at eight triggered suggestions. A genuinely gap-free pilot with no stated ambitions would trigger five (four always plus test_fly_first), still at max_shown. The pool cannot drop below four for any answer set.
suggestion_coverage.step_confidence_suggestion: 'judge_the_wing_not_the_label' is priority 12, so it backfills rather than crowding out earned advice, and most personas here will not see it displayed. That is intentional but matters MORE at this step than at any below, because the contested-boundary finding is this step's headline. The same honesty reaches every pilot unconditionally through always_output.methodology_note and always_output.instructor_recommendation in the scoring config, and through meta.confidence_statement_for_ui in the questions config. Owner call if it should be promoted — this is the strongest case in the ladder for promoting it.
suggestion_coverage.high_priority_siv_suggestion: 'siv_before_you_upgrade' is priority 1 with the broadest trigger of any SIV suggestion in the ladder (no practice beyond theory, OR no real collapse handled, OR no course done). Personas 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07 and 09 all trigger it; only 01 and 08 don't, and both have two courses plus current practice plus a real asymmetric flown out. It remains entirely non-scored: the only thing SIV touches numerically is the capped 2-point bonus, unchanged from all three steps below. Persona 02 is the proof — she reaches Ready with no course at all, and her total clears the threshold before the bonus is added.
suggestion_coverage.new_at_this_step: Five suggestions exist only at this step: 'site_variety_build' and 'xc_experience_build' (the first-ever scored treatment of USHPA P4's site-variety and BHPA's XC-distance figures), 'effort_sunk_cost' (paired with the new effort_already_invested question), 'resale_and_cost' (the financial half of the asymmetric-risk finding) and 'performance_chasing_reframe' (Passion Paragliding's argument, fired only when the performance motive is paired with no limiting evidence). Coverage: site_variety_build 05/06/07, xc_experience_build 03/05/06/07, effort_sunk_cost 06/08, resale_and_cost 03/04/05/06/08/09, performance_chasing_reframe — NOT exercised as a firing suggestion, deliberately. Personas 03 and 04 both answer 'I want more glide and speed' and both can name the flights their wing cost them, so the second half of its trigger is false for both; a synthetic check should confirm it fires for 'want_more_performance' plus 'not_really'.

negative_checks: No persona may be gated or band-dropped for not having done a manoeuvres course. Persona 02 reaches Ready with 'manoeuvre_course: no' and her total clears the threshold of 78 BEFORE the 2-point bonus is added; persona 07 reaches Nearly ready without one; persona 08 stays Not yet having done two. knowledge/disagreements.md point 1 and BRIEF.md both require SIV to be a small positive signal only — and this is the step where the pro-SIV sources are most emphatic, so this check matters more here than anywhere below.

The collapse gate must never become an SIV gate. 'collapse_response_entirely_untested' is cleared by SELF-practice (pulling and releasing tip folds alone) and separately by having caught a real collapse. A synthetic check should confirm that a pilot with 'collapse_practice: some_self_practice' and 'collapse_experience: never' is NOT gated — only held at Nearly ready by the collapse_practice Ready-blocker. If that ever starts capping, the rubric has quietly introduced a course requirement the brief forbids.

Neither new question may gate or Ready-block. Persona 07 answers 'home site only' and 'no cross-country yet' and is neither gated nor caught by the critical_check_floor — the two answers cost him about five points of skills and nothing else. knowledge/steps/high-b-to-low-c.md's own caveat calls these "supporting, non-gating signals at this step", and knowledge/disagreements.md point 14 adds Joy Paragliding arguing against tying wing upgrades to kilometres at all. A scorer that blocks Ready on either has turned a pilot-rating requirement into a wing-class gate.

No stated-plans exemption may fire at this step. Every persona's exemptions list is empty, and config/scoring/high-b-to-low-c.json ships an empty exemptions array with its reasoning recorded. A scorer that shares exemption logic across steps, or falls back to a sibling step's config, will wrongly exempt a soaring-only pilot here. This is the single most likely cross-step regression, same as at mid-B to high-B.

A pilot who reports no collapse history must not be penalised into a lower band for it. Persona 02 answers 'collapse_experience: never' and reaches Ready; the answer scores exactly 0.5, which is the critical_check_floor minimum, so it passes rather than being excused. Persona 07 gives the same answer and is held by his skills category score, not by this. The markdown from 0.55 one rung below must not drift further.

A pilot who regularly flies strong thermic and mountain days must not be scored down for it. Personas 01 and 08 both answer 'strong_mountain_big_air' and it takes a full 1.0, as at mid-B to high-B. Note the related change in the other direction: 'proper thermic days, fairly regularly' drops from 1.0 to 0.9 here, because this step's sources ask for genuinely turbulent thermic air specifically. Personas 02, 03, 04 and 07 all pay that single point.

Ambition alone may never cost a band. Persona 01 ticks longer_xc and reaches Ready; persona 03 ticks longer_xc and is held only by thermic hours; persona 05 ticks longer_xc with skills a few points above 55 and is NOT gated by it; persona 08 ticks longer_xc and competitions with skills near 99 and is NOT gated by it. Only persona 06, who pairs them with a skills score in the thirties, is. Persona 05's margin is deliberately small and is the one to re-check if the skills weights ever change.

Wanting more performance must never be penalised on its own, per knowledge/disagreements.md point 9. Personas 03 and 04 both answer 'want_more_performance' and neither is gated for it; the answer is marked down one notch to 0.7 on Passion Paragliding's step-specific argument and takes part in no gate. 'performance_chasing_reframe' requires the motive AND no limiting evidence, which is why neither of them triggers it.

A comparison-driven motive must not cap a pilot whose readiness evidence is genuinely there. Persona 08 matches the 'equipment_as_a_fix_with_thin_readiness' motive clause twice over and must NOT be gated, because every branch of its readiness clause is false. Personas 05 and 06 are where the same gate correctly fires, with the same kind of motive and genuinely thin readiness.

An injury or reserve deployment in the last 12 months must not cap a result on its own. No persona here answers 'incidents_12m: injury_or_reserve' — worth a synthetic check that such a pilot, otherwise strong, is NOT gated and does trigger 'post_collapse_support'. Carried forward from config/scoring/a-to-low-b.json's v2 removal of exactly that gate.

An untroubled answer about rough air must not be read as a fear problem. Persona 08 answers 'it doesn't really bother me' and 'nerves_are_not_the_problem' must NOT fire for him — its trigger is freezing or tensing up. The answer scores 0.5, exactly on the Ready-blocker line, which is flagged as a judgement rather than a finding in meta.owner_decisions.

No rule, gate or suggestion message may present the thermal-hours figure as a single number, or claim the high-B/low-C distinction is settled. The hours range is 75 to 100-plus and one retailer's own two articles disagree (knowledge/disagreements.md points 2 and 6); the boundary is the most contested on the ladder (point 3). Read every fired message in personas 03, 06 and 09 against that, plus the 'build_thermic_hours' suggestion — those are the four places most likely to drift.

No message may repeat the 'roughly half of EN-C pilots shouldn't be on them' line as a statistic. It is one author's own estimate, not a study. The gate message, the rule message and three suggestions all touch this material and all say 'a large share' or 'a lot of pilots' instead. Personas 05 and 09 are the ones who see it.
Every pilot must reach at least three displayed suggestions. Enforced for all nine personas by the displayed-count invariant in scripts/check-personas.mts; all nine reach five.

Nothing in a Ready or Nearly ready output may read as talking a hesitant pilot into the upgrade. Persona 02 is the one to read for this — she is capable, careful and correct to be, and docs/design-context.md's safety guard forbids reassurance as a design goal. Personas 03 and 07 are the second and third: both are strong pilots being told 'not for this wing, not yet' for a specific, narrow reason, and both results have to land as information rather than as a reprimand.

chain_notes.merge_behaviour: In a mid-B to low-C chain (config/questions/mid-b-to-high-b.json then config/questions/high-b-to-low-c.json), 31 of this step's 34 questions are byte-identical to their counterparts at the step below and merge into a single screen each, so the chain asks 32 + 34 - 31 = 35 questions rather than 66. The three that deliberately do NOT merge are wing_expectation (its text names the target class and its middle option describes this class's specific demand), xc_experience (new) and effort_already_invested (new). Note what this means and why it is deliberate: the hours bands, and the ground-handling, speed-bar and collapse-practice option scales, are NOT re-scaled at this step even though the wing class is a rung higher. Re-scaling them would have produced three or four near-identical back-to-back screens in a chained run, and no source at this step gives a figure to re-scale toward. The scores behind those identical options ARE a band harder here, which is exactly what per-leg scoring is for — see config/scoring/high-b-to-low-c.json meta.design_decisions 'v1-hours-bands-reused-from-the-step-below' for the two straddles that choice accepts.
chain_notes.verification: The 31/3 split was verified by extracting every question id, question text and option label from both files and comparing them line by line, not by trusting the CHAIN MERGE note in the questions config. scripts/check-merge-rule.mts does not yet contain a 'mid-b-to-high-b -> high-b-to-low-c' entry — adding one is build work, and the expectedMergedIds list should be re-derived independently at that point rather than copied from this note, which is the convention the previous two rungs followed. The mustNotMergeIds list for that pair is ['wing_expectation'] (xc_experience and effort_already_invested cannot merge because they exist at only one step, so they need no assertion).
chain_notes.what_a_chain_persona_would_need_to_check: That a merged answer is scored against EACH step's own bands when a full pilot profile runs an A-to-low-C or mid-B-to-low-C chain. The most visible cases at this rung are 'active_piloting: work_brakes_actively' (0.9 at low-B to mid-B, 0.7 at mid-B to high-B, 0.6 here), 'collapse_practice: some_self_practice' (0.6 at mid-B to high-B and passing, 0.45 here and Ready-blocking), 'thermic_airtime: 25_50' (0.6 and passing one rung down, 0.3 and Ready-blocking here) and 'site_variety: home_site_only' (0.4 and near-inert one rung down, 0.2 at weight 9 here). tests/personas/chains/ currently has fixtures up to the third rung; a fourth extending them through this leg would close the gap.
chain_notes.registry: config/scoring, config/questions and config/suggestions for this step exist, but app/upgrade/lib/ladder.ts STEP_REGISTRY does not yet list 'high-b-to-low-c': { from: 'high-B', to: 'low-C' }. Until it does, resolveChain returns null for any target above high-B and the picker will not offer low-C. Adding the registry entry is build work, not rubric work, and is listed here so it is not missed.
chain_notes.source: BRIEF.md 'Multi-step jumps' and its recorded implementation trap: question ids are not safe to treat as globally shared, and the merge must compare actual option sets rather than ids.
